title: Ovarian Functional Decline Across the Reproductive Lifespan: The SOFI-M Framework for Precision Phenotyping, Prevention, and Therapeutic Matching
content: Ovarian functional decline encompasses physiological reproductive aging, diminished ovarian reserve (DOR), poor ovarian response (POR), iatrogenic injury, and premature ovarian insufficiency (POI). These phenotypes can arise from different combinations of follicle depletion, impaired oocyte competence, dysregulated activation, mitochondrial dysfunction, immune remodeling, vascular injury, and stromal fibrosis; no single reju-venation principle can address all states. This critical narrative review integrates evidence available through October 2026 and proposes a precision framework separating protec-tion, follicle activation, niche repair, competence support, and functional replacement. The Segmented Ovarian Function Impairment Matrix (SOFI-M) records eight graded domains with confidence and longitudinal direction. Treatment is represented as an ac-tive-component vector matched to lesion profile, host biology, and therapeutic window. The framework is applied to molecular pharmacotherapy, platelet-rich plasma, stromal and hematopoietic cell products, extracellular vesicles, biomaterials, chromo-some-cohesion rescue, and cryopreserved ovarian tissue. Preliminary human ex vivo SGO1 target engagement is reported only in a preprint and conference abstract, while clinical evidence for other emerging strategies remains inconsistent or uncontrolled. Current data do not establish reversal of ovarian aging, restoration of the primordial pool, or cumulative live-birth benefit. Defined phenotypes and products, mechanistic end-points, controlled trials, and long-term maternal and offspring surveillance are required before routine use.
